newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Proton to roll out 1 millionth car.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Proton to roll out 1 millionth car.

text.p: After 11 years of production, Malaysia's first national car maker Proton is set to roll out its 1 millionth vehicle on Monday.

The guest of honour at the at the ceremony at Proton's production plant in Shah Alam -- an industrial area just outside capital city Kuala Lumpur -- will be Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, the mastermind behind the car project.
Mahathir is also expected to unveil a new 1.8-litre coupe.
Though the road ahead may be slightly bumpy, analysts say the company was likely to motor along without too many breakdowns.

Already, Proton's acquisition of British sports car maker Lotus Group International Ltd. in October for 51 million British pounds ($85 million) has put it in good stead to develop its own engines and transmission systems.

"In the early years the emphasis was on production. They just wanted to produce as many cars as possible, and since it is a protected market, they did not worry too much about (developing) their own technology," said Choo Swee Kee, analyst at equities research house Vickers Ballas in Kuala Lumpur.

Proton (Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd) makes family saloon cars named Saga, Iswara, Wira and Perdana, and a three-door hatchback, Satria. In Europe, the Wira is called Persona and the Satria, the Persona Compact.
When the first Proton rolled off the production lines in 1985 in a venture with Japan's Mitsubishi Motors Corp., the company was at the vanguard of Mahathir's industrialisation programme.
As such the Malaysian government made sure that Proton was protected from competition from foreign car makers by slapping on a 300 percent import tariff.
But international trade agreements will bring down tariffs on foreign imported cars by 1998, forcing Proton to cut costs as one way to become more competitive.
Another way to achieve greater economies of scale is by producing more cars. Proton plans to turn out 230,000 cars a year by end of 1997 from 180,000 currently.
The company has also been aggressively marketing the cars overseas, pitting them against more experienced Japanese and European car makers.
